audit.why: 48.43% over 1053 games — a large sample and a genuinely losing lane for Ambessa.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Ambessa four of seven stages on a lane she loses at 48.43%, and it contradicts five of its own why-lines: whys[1] says Karma 'beats your trade attempts before 6' where the chart says Skill; whys[2] says 'genuinely coin-flip' where the chart says Ambessa; whys[3] calls 4-5 'your weakest window' where the chart says Ambessa; whys[5] says 'it's a coin flip' where the chart says Ambessa; whys[6] says 'she reclaims the lane' where the chart says Ambessa. It also marks level 6 for Karma, the one stage whys[4] describes as Ambessa flipping the all-in.
audit.why: This is a poke lane. Karma owns everything except the single window where a 1250-unit suppress exists, and even the first-item stage is conditional on her Mantra being down.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Karma / Karma / Skill / Karma / Ambessa / Skill / Karma in both layers — Karma 4, Skill 2, Ambessa 1, which fits 48.43% and matches every why on the page.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says 'she has no hard lockdown until her Mantra-empowered Q comes online at 6'. Riot's text ends with: 'Mantra is available at level 1 and does not require a skill point.' Karma has her empowered ability from the first wave. Ambessa's level 6 is also credited to 'the passive armor-pen plus on-damage heal', which is in Riot's text for none of her abilities.
audit.why: Telling a player they have five safe levels before the enemy's ultimate exists is the most dangerous kind of error on a coaching page — it licenses exactly the walk-up that gets punished. Karma's real spike curve is flat and early: Mantra from level 1 on 40/38/36/34s, shortened further by Gathering Fire whenever her damaging abilities land.
audit.corrected: Mantra's level-1 availability stated in early, spikes[0].text and the level 6 phase. Gathering Fire's cooldown reduction added to whys[1], mid and breakdown.cooldowns. Penetration and healing claims on Ambessa's R removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer attributes Karma's root to the wrong ability in five separate fields. It repeatedly calls it 'her RQ-root', 'her Mantra-empowered Q (RQ): it roots and tethers you', 'past the range her RQ-root needs', 'her RQ tether'. Riot's text: the root is Focused Resolve (W) — 'creates a tether between herself and a targeted enemy... If the tether is not broken, the enemy will be rooted'. Mantra on Q creates a delayed cataclysm; Mantra on W is what extends the root and heals her. The full layer already names Focused Resolve correctly, so the two layers of the same matchup disagree.
audit.why: The counterplay is completely different depending on which ability it is. Focused Resolve is a 675-range tether on a flat 12 seconds that only converts into a root IF THE TETHER IS NOT BROKEN — and Ambessa has three dashes plus terrain to break it with. A player told the root comes from her ultimate will hold their dash for a 40-second cooldown that is not the threat, and eat a 12-second one they could have walked out of.
audit.corrected: All five references corrected to Focused Resolve with the 12s / 675-range figures, and the break-the-tether counterplay stated in mid, spikes[3].text, wants.you[0], report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Inner Flame is described only as out-ranging your cone, with no numbers on either side.
audit.why: 950 against Cunning Sweep's 650 is a 300-unit gap on a 9-second cooldown falling to 5 — that is the whole reason the early game is unwinnable rather than merely hard, and it makes the number worth printing.
audit.corrected: 950 vs 650 stated in whys[0], early, spikes[0].text and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer's content mentions Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: Mantra-empowered Focused Resolve heals Karma while extending the root, so the ability that locks you down also refills her. In a lane you are already losing on poke, that heal is what makes the one trade you do win not matter.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal added to wants.you[2] and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Gathering Fire is never mentioned, and the tether's break condition was only in the full layer.
audit.why: Gathering Fire means Karma's Mantra cooldown is not fixed — every damaging ability that lands shortens it, so poking you is how she pays for her next empowered cast. Combined with the tether break rule, these are the two mechanics that tell an Ambessa player what to actually do: deny the poke, and dash out of the tether.
audit.corrected: Both added to the content layer.

edits.before: Karma owns the opening — her Inner Flame (Q) outranges your Cunning Sweep cone and your dash only fires off the back of an ability cast, so every walk-up to last-hit trades health for a creep. Do not try to fight through her poke at Levels 1-2; your cooldowns are long and you can't reliably stick to her once she pops E for the move speed. Last-hit at range, lean on the empowered auto from your passive stacks for safe poke-back, and brace Repudiation (W) into her Q so the blocked damage amps your next hit. The one mercy is she has no hard lockdown until her Mantra-empowered Q comes online at 6.
edits.after: Karma owns the opening — Inner Flame (Q) reaches 950 against your 650 cone and your dash only fires off the back of an ability cast, so every walk-up to last-hit trades health for a creep. Do not try to fight through her poke at Levels 1-2; your cooldowns are long and Inspire (E) hands her a shield and move speed the moment you commit. Last-hit at range, lean on the empowered auto from your passive stacks, and brace Repudiation into her Q so the blocked damage amps your next hit. And know that Mantra is available from level 1 and costs no skill point — the empowered cast exists from wave one.

edits.before: Through Levels 4-5 you're still conceding — her poke compounds and you have no way to commit safely. Then Level 6 is your one real flip: Public Execution blinks you behind the farthest target in your chosen line, past the range her RQ-root needs, suppresses and stuns, and the passive armor-pen plus on-damage heal lets you actually finish. Bait her E shield or her RQ first, then R in and chain Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam with your empowered autos. If you dump R while her Mantra is up to peel, she roots you, kites the suppression's end, and takes the lane back.
edits.after: Through Levels 4-5 you're still conceding — her poke compounds and Gathering Fire shortens Mantra every time a damaging ability lands. Level 6 is your one real flip: Public Execution blinks 1250 units to the farthest champion in your chosen line, suppresses, then slams her down stunned. The root is Focused Resolve (W), flat 12 seconds at 675 range, and it only converts if the tether survives — a Drakehound's Step out of range or behind terrain breaks it first. Bait Inspire's shield, then R and chain Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam.

edits.before: This stays a fight against her range. Your first-item Eclipse spike with Q gives real kill threat when your R is up, but once she has two items of poke and her RQ tether to peel, she reclaims the lane — she chips you out before you can ever commit and your physical-only damage does nothing against her E shield while she sits behind minions. Pick your all-ins around her Mantra cooldown and her flash, and accept that if you don't snowball off a Level 6 R, she scales into a poke-and-peel problem you can't catch.
edits.after: This stays a fight against her range. Your first-item Eclipse spike gives real kill threat when your R is up, but two items of poke plus Focused Resolve's 12-second tether let her chip you out before you can ever commit, and Inspire's shield soaks the front of every combo. Buy Grievous Wounds — a Mantra-empowered tether heals her while it extends the root. Pick your all-ins around Mantra's 40 seconds and her flash, and accept that without a Level 6 snowball she scales past you.

notes: This page had the most dangerous single error in my slice: 'she has no hard lockdown until her Mantra-empowered Q comes online at 6'. Riot's own text for Mantra ends 'Mantra is available at level 1 and does not require a skill point', so Karma is empowered from the first wave. Compounding it, the content layer attributed her root to Mantra-Q in five places when it belongs to Focused Resolve (W) — and the FULL layer of the same matchup already named Focused Resolve correctly, so the two halves of one page disagreed about which ability roots you. Worth checking every Karma matchup in the repo for both errors. The packet's suspectNames flagged 'Her Inner Flame' as a probable wrong name; it is the correct name and a false positive, while the two real errors on the page went unflagged. Unverified and removed rather than restated: Ambessa's 'passive armor-pen' and 'on-damage heal'. Cosmetic issue I left alone: the full layer refers to Karma as 'his'/'he' in tldr, winCon, tradeGood, breakdown.mid and breakdown.feeding — template pronoun leakage that runs across this whole file.
